title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): for fields of finite type over Q, Grothendieck expects K -> B_K (the étale topos of Spec K, i.e. the classifying topos of the absolute Galois group), K -> Pi_K (the profinite fundamental groupoid) and (K, Kbar) -> E_{Kbar/K} (the Galois group) to be 'fully faithful', or at least to detect isomorphisms. This is the birational anabelian conjecture. For arbitrary fields this fails badly: a separably closed field gives the point topos, the trivial groupoid and the trivial group, so morphisms between separably closed fields are invisible.

This page proposes the fix. Attach to K the projective system (pro-object) (B_{K_i}), or (Pi_{K_i}), indexed by the subfields K_i of K of finite type over the prime field. For a pair (K, Kbar), attach the pro-system (E_{Kbar_i/K_i}), where Kbar_i is the separable closure of K_i in Kbar.

The limits of these systems give back the classical invariants (1):
- Pi_K = lim Pi_{K_i};
- B_K = lim B_{K_i};
- E_{Kbar/K} = lim E_{Kbar_i/K_i}.
So the classical objects are 'reconstituted' from the pro-systems. The image most plausibly reads 'mais l'inverse n'est pas vrai': the converse fails, since the limit forgets the pro-structure, and that pro-structure is the finer information wanted.

The key formal point: Ind(fields of finite type) -> Fields is an equivalence. This is 'trivial' because:
- every field is the filtered union of its finitely generated subfields;
- a field of finite type is a compact (finitely presentable) object in the category of fields, field maps being injective.
Hence any (2-)functor defined on fields of finite type extends canonically to all fields, with values in Pro(topoi / profinite groupoids / profinite groups). The extension inherits all the full-faithfulness properties of the restricted functor, because Hom_Pro((X_i), (Y_j)) = lim_j colim_i Hom(X_i, Y_j).

The next page states this conclusion explicitly. It then decides to restrict to absolutely finitely generated fields, while noting the need for a purely algebraic description of the fundamental pro-groups attached to (C, Cbar). In modern terms: a field K is recovered (in the anabelian sense) from the pro-system of absolute Galois groups of its finitely generated subfields. This reduces the anabelian program for arbitrary fields to Pop's theorem for finitely generated fields.
errors: No mathematical error. The formulas (1) are correct: Galois group of a filtered union of fields = inverse limit of Galois groups; étale topos of a filtered limit of qcqs schemes with affine transitions = limit of the topoi (SGA4 VII); the profinite-groupoid 2-limit is well behaved because lim^1 of compact groups vanishes.

The machine reading 'l'assertion n'est pas vraie' would make the page claim (1) is false, which is wrong. The intended reading is almost certainly 'l'inverse n'est pas vrai': the pro-system cannot be recovered from its limit.

Implicit gap: the functors are 2-functors (to topoi / groupoids, with Homs defined up to inner automorphism / 2-isomorphism). 'Pro' must be taken in a 2-categorical sense, and pro-objects in 2-categories need care. Grothendieck passes over this. Also, 'fully faithful' for morphisms rather than isomorphisms on finitely generated fields is stronger than what Pop proved (an isomorphism version, with Hom-versions partially by Mochizuki).

ideas.what: Replace B_K / Pi_K / Gal(Kbar/K) of an arbitrary field by the pro-system of the corresponding invariants of its finitely generated subfields, to repair non-faithfulness (e.g. for separably closed fields)
ideas.modern_name: Pro-extension of the birational anabelian functor; Galois pro-invariants of a field
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (implicit in the anabelian program); not a standard named construction
ideas.where_published: Probably in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (Malgoire edition, Montpellier 1995), of which this manuscript is the draft/source

ideas.what: Gal(Kbar/K) = lim Gal(Kbar_i/K_i), and étale topos of Spec K = limit of étale topoi of Spec K_i
ideas.modern_name: Continuity of Galois groups / étale topoi under filtered limits
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; SGA4 exposé VII for topoi
ideas.where_published: SGA4 VII (limits of topoi); standard Galois theory

ideas.what: Fields = Ind(fields of finite type), so functors on finitely generated fields extend to Pro-valued functors on all fields preserving full faithfulness
ideas.modern_name: Ind-completion / compact generation of the category of fields; Pro-extension of fully faithful functors
ideas.where_published: SGA4 exposé I (Ind-objects); applied here to the anabelian setting

ideas.what: Fully faithful (or isomorphism-detecting) Galois functor on fields of finite type over Q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, letter to Faltings 1983); Neukirch–Uchida for number fields; Pop 1994 for finitely generated fields over Q; Pop later in positive characteristic
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

missed.claim: A Pro-valued anabelian invariant of an arbitrary field: K |-> 'lim' G_{K_i} over finitely generated subfields K_i. This inherits Pop's theorem, so every field of characteristic 0 is anabelian in this pro-sense (at least for isomorphisms). The literature generally restricts to finitely generated fields, or uses other devices for fields over algebraically closed bases (Bogomolov–Pop pro-l abelian-by-central). This explicit pro-formulation is rarely stated, but it is a formal consequence and would not surprise specialists.
missed.quote: il y a lieu d'associer à un corps K un objet plus fin que B_K ou Pi_K, à savoir le système projectif des B_{K_i}, ou des Pi_{K_i}, pour K_i sous-corps de K de type fini sur le corps premier
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a clean formal framework, namely 2-pro-objects of profinite groupoids, in which anabelian statements for arbitrary fields (e.g. C as an extension of Q) can be phrased. It connects to the later need, stated on the next page, for an algebraic description of the pro-groups attached to (C, Cbar). It is minor, as it is formal.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clear but formal step: it uses Ind/Pro completion to extend the anabelian functor from finitely generated fields to all fields. Correct and characteristic of Grothendieck, but routine for specialists, and likely reproduced in the Malgoire edition of La Longue Marche.
transcription_corrections: 'mais l'assertion n'est pas vraie' should most likely read 'mais l'inverse n'est pas vrai' (the converse is not true); this changes the mathematical meaning.
In the third formula the right-hand side is written E_{Kbar_i/K_i} (the handwriting looks like 'F' but is E).
In the last line the second listed functor is preceded by 'ou' ('ou K -> Pi_K, ou (K,Kbar) -> E_{Kbar/K}, elles...').
